description: Na₄Mg(FeO₂)₄ crystallizes in the monoclinic C2 space group. There are three inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to four O atoms. There are two shorter (2.46 Å) and two longer (2.81 Å) Na-O bond lengths. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to four O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.11-2.37 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded to four O atoms to form distorted NaO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent FeO₄ tetrahedra and  an edgeedge with one FeO₄ tetrahedra. There are two shorter (2.35 Å) and two longer (2.40 Å) Na-O bond lengths. Mg is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Mg-O bond distances ranging from 2.12-2.45 Å. There are three inequivalent Fe sites. In the first Fe site, Fe is bonded to four O atoms to form FeO₄ tetrahedra that share  an edgeedge with one NaO₄ tetrahedra. There are two shorter (1.90 Å) and two longer (1.96 Å) Fe-O bond lengths. In the second Fe site, Fe is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to four O atoms. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.90-2.15 Å. In the third Fe site, Fe is bonded to four O atoms to form FeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaO₄ tetrahedra. There are two shorter (1.88 Å) and two longer (1.98 Å) Fe-O bond lengths. There are four inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded to two Na, one Mg, and two Fe atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing ONa₂MgFe₂ trigonal bipyramids. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na and two Fe atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Mg, and two Fe atoms. In the fourth O site, O is bonded to two Na, one Mg, and two Fe atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing ONa₂MgFe₂ trigonal bipyramids.
